 Cologne struggling this season published at 19:26 GMT 19:26 GMT 
 Bayern Munich v Cologne (19:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Cologne have struggled this season, they sit in 15th place with just nine points from their nine games played this season.
 Cologne have struggled on the road this season with Rene Wagner’s side only picking up one point from four away games so far and only scoring three goals in the process.
 Cologne’s record against Bayern isn’t one to shout from the rooftops either; Cologne hasn’t beaten Bayern in 22 games. The last time they tasted victory over the Bavarian’s was in 2011.
 1 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Kompany expected to make his return published at 19:25 GMT 19:25 GMT 
 Bayern Munich v Cologne (19:30 BST) 
 Image source, Getty Images Bayern Munich have picked up where they left off last season, extending their unbeaten run in the Bundesliga to 24 games. They sit top of the Bundesliga with 21 points and a goal difference of plus 20 thanks to six wins and three draws in the previous nine matchdays.
 Bayern’s only defeat in 41 competitive matches came in the Champions League semi-final against eventual winners Paris Saint Germain.
 Bayern’s impressive start to the season has come despite the absence of head coach Vincent Kompany.
 Kompany collapsed during training a month ago and was later diagnosed with meningreal irritation meaning he has been absent from the sidelines for the last five games with assistant Aaron Danks stepping.
 Kompany is expected to make his return for Friday’s match at the Allianz Arena.

 Welcome, Bundesliga is back! published at 19:03 GMT 19:03 GMT 
 Bayern Munich v Cologne (19:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images After a busy international break the Bundesliga is back on the BBC on Friday night and we’re heading to Bavaria to see Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich. 
 The first match after the November International break is an intriguing match up between a Bayern side who lead the Bundesliga on goal difference over Borussia Dortmund and a Cologne side who finished last season in fourteenth after a one-year spell in Bundesliga 2 in 2024/25.
 The home side are the only team across Europe’s top five divisions to not lose a competitive fixture in 2026/27. Meanwhile their opponents can feel themselves hard done to after some of their performances haven’t earned the points expected. 
 Cologne sits in eleventh place in the Bundesliga table for big chances created and sixth for big chances missed, meaning that The Billy Goats could well be higher up the table than they currently are.
